scenario: AITA for not hosting thanksgiving like I planned to | For about 50 years, my mom hosted all of her children and grandchildren for thanksgiving and Christmas Eve. She’s now gotten too old and asked us kids to take over the tradition. There are 4 of us so we just rotate. We’ve each hosted one holiday so far. This thanksgiving is my turn. We have never spent thanksgiving or Christmas Eve with my wife’s family. We’ve just never been as close to them plus they live all over the country. Well this year her mom and aunts decided to go to the Macy’s thanksgiving day parade. At first it was just a sister’s trip but then they decided to invite all their kids and grandkids to meet them up there. My wife really wants to go. She hasnt seen some of her aunts and cousins in years. Our daughter wants to go because it’s a “once in a lifetime event” (which i agree with). And I want to go. As soon as we decided to go I called my older brother to see what we should do about thanksgiving because I can’t host this year. He said our oldest sister is going to be pissed and i have to tell her myself. He wished me luck. So I call her and she is mad. She says she’ll probably have to end up hosting even though she is up next for Christmas and I’m being inconsiderate of what our mom asked us to do. “Mom wouldn’t abandon thanksgiving to go to nyc” and went on about how sad mom will be that I’m doing this. I offered to pay for them to rent a spot and have it catered but she said that takes away from the close knit family vibe. My brother said his wife might be up for it but he didn’t sound too happy about asking her. My other sister can’t do it because she’s renovating her house. I do feel bad for backing out of my turn but I tried to offer up solutions and I also offered to host the next holiday—which my oldest sister said no to because it’s her turn and she’s been planning for it all year. Next up is my brother so I said me and him could maybe just swap thanksgivings if his wife is up for it. Am I in the wrong here?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I'm in the wrong here. Let me start by understanding the situation. My mom used to host Thanksgiving and Christmas Eve for all her kids and grandkids for about 50 years. Now she's too old, so we, the four kids, take turns hosting. Each of us has already hosted one holiday so far. This year, it's my turn to host Thanksgiving. But here's the thing: my wife's family decided to go to the Macy's Thanksgiving Day parade. They invited all their kids and grandkids, and my wife really wants to go. Our daughter also wants to go because it's a once-in-a-lifetime event. I want to go too. So, we decided to go, and then I called my older brother to figure out what to do about Thanksgiving since I can't host this year. He said our oldest sister is going to be mad and that I have to tell her myself. He wished me luck. When I called her, she was mad. She said she'll probably have to end up hosting even though it's her turn for Christmas. She accused me of being inconsiderate of what our mom asked us to do. She also mentioned that Mom would be sad if I abandon Thanksgiving to go to New York. I offered to pay for them to rent a place and have it catered, but she said that takes away from the close-knit family vibe. My brother mentioned his wife might be up for hosting, but he didn't sound too happy about asking her. My other sister can't host because she's renovating her house. I feel bad about backing out of my turn, but I tried to offer solutions. I also offered to host the next holiday, but my oldest sister said no because it's her turn and she's been planning it all year. Next up is my brother, so I suggested swapping Thanksgiving if his wife is up for it. Now, I'm wondering if I'm in the wrong here. Hmm, so the main issue is that I'm breaking the tradition by not hosting Thanksgiving this year because I want to go to the parade with my wife's family. My sister is upset because she was expecting to host Christmas, not Thanksgiving. My mom would be disappointed, and the family vibe is important to her. I tried to offer solutions, like paying for a venue and catering, but she didn't like that idea. I also offered to host the next holiday, but she refused. I think the key points are: respecting the family tradition, considering everyone's feelings, and trying to find a compromise. I want to spend time with my wife's family, but I also don't want to upset my sister or make my mom sad. I tried to be responsible by offering solutions, but they didn't work out. Maybe I should have communicated better or found another way to make it work. I'm not sure if I'm in the wrong. On one hand, I have a valid reason to want to go to the parade with my family. On the other hand, I'm breaking the tradition that our mom started, and my sister is upset because she was counting on hosting Christmas. I feel like I did the right thing by trying to find solutions, but maybe I should have been more flexible or found another way to accommodate both. In the end, I think I'm not entirely in the wrong, but I could have handled it better. Maybe I should have talked to my sister earlier or found a way to make it work without making her host again. But I did try to offer help, so I'm not sure.
